name: Unnamed blockchain organization post-termination sabotage attempt

attribution.legal_posture: DTEX-described, DPRK-affiliated post-termination incident at an unnamed blockchain organization; attribution is vendor-stated and independently uncorroborated in public records

caveats: Attribution is DTEX's statement; the organization and workers are unnamed, and independent public incident-record status is unreported.
The record excludes code, repository locator, credentials, internal system details, and victim-identifying data.
The separate Top 2000 engineer logic-bomb case is described later in the advisory; its relationship to DPRK activity is unreported, so incident records stay separate.
The unrelated Top 2000 logic-bomb case in the same advisory is outside DPRK attribution and this record.

statements: DTEX states that, while working with affected organizations, it observed post-termination activity by workers it described as DPRK-affiliated targeting critical infrastructure at an unnamed blockchain entity.

The dismissed workers allegedly tried to regain access to the main database and execute code intended to sabotage the system; DTEX says the attempt failed because the employer revoked privileges in time.
The case supports immediate access revocation, session and token invalidation, credential rotation, and focused post-termination monitoring for privileged remote workers.
